description: Over the first 8,000 lines of a real compile log the fz output differs from Elixir's in the 'cause of every wake' table. Cause (verified by diffing with padding removed): cause_table in tools/distill-telemetry.exs does Enum.frequencies |> Enum.sort_by(fn {_, n} -> -n end) |> Enum.take(top). Rows with equal counts keep the map's iteration order, and the map has more than 32 keys, so Elixir's order is its hash order and fz's is its own; take(top) then keeps different tied rows (4 rows differ, 2 swap places), which also changes a column width. Not a miscompile. Two ways out: the script sorts by a total key ({-n, key}), which makes both runtimes agree whatever the map order; or fz reproduces Elixir's order for maps past 32 keys (the open map-order question). The pinned 112 KB trace does not reach this. Repro: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz-xxd13-build/d6960461-b7a2-4585-a9e7-9f2477e57ee2/scratchpad/slow/h8000.jsonl, out8000.txt (fz), ex8000.txt (elixir).
title: Map iteration order decides which tied rows the distiller's wake table keeps
